title: Raw approve with an unchecked boolean return in the ERC4626YieldStrategy constructor
description: IERC20(_underlyingToken).approve(_erc4626Vault, type(uint256).max); at ERC4626YieldStrategy.sol:50. USDT's approve returns no data, so a bool-decoding call reverts. This is the only unguarded ERC20 call in src/.
impact: Deployment fails against USDT-like tokens. The failure is DEPLOY-TIME AND LOUD — nothing deploys — which is why it is QA and not a footgun.
attackPath: The strategy is deployed with a USDT-like underlying token whose approve returns no data.
The constructor's bool-decoding approve call reverts.
Deployment fails loudly. Nothing is silently mis-wired.
recommendation: One line: use SafeERC20.forceApprove instead of the raw approve.
invalidHeadingsTested: Approve race / safeApprove front-running — DOES NOT APPLY. That invalid covers the ERC20 allowance double-spend across an approve(x) -> approve(y) transition. This is a SINGLE ONE-SHOT approve inside the constructor, the spender is the strategy's own configured _erc4626Vault (validated non-zero on the line above), there is no second approve and no allowance transition anywhere in the contract, and the code runs at deployment so there is no transaction to front-run. The asserted failure mode is a bool-decode revert on a token that returns no data — a different defect entirely.

Non-standard/weird ERC-20 (except USDT) — DOES NOT APPLY, because USDT IS THE EXPLICIT CARVE-OUT AND USDT IS THE TOKEN THAT TRIPS THIS. The carve-out is the finding's BASIS, not a suppression of it. The finding rests on USDT specifically and invokes no other token quirk — no rebasing, no deflationary, no fee-on-transfer leg.
lawBasis: Law 3 correctly NOT invoked: the failure is deploy-time and loud, so it fails the surprise test. QA is the right severity.
supportingContext: CFG-01 / 0c12a2cfaf4b026a (open) is evidence the wired-vault configuration has already been wrong once.
